cohort: 72 women with pregnancy-induced hypertension who delivered low-birth-weight babies, divided into two groups of 36 based on mode of delivery (vaginal vs. cesarean).
finding: Neonatal outcomes were not significantly different between vaginal and cesarean deliveries in women with well-controlled hypertension.
mod_finding: While there were numerical differences in some neonatal complications between vaginal and cesarean deliveries, these were not statistically significant, suggesting that mode of birth did not significantly affect these outcomes in the context of well-controlled maternal hypertension.
followup_time: Early neonatal period (likely within the first few days of life)
birth_weight: Low birth weight (specific weight range not provided)
